To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ESBL/pAmpsC-EC were subdominant in the broiler chain and that their prevalence is overestimated by selective media.
the prevalence and genetic composition of ESBL/p AmpC-producing Eschericia coli (ESBL/ pAmpC- E. coli) in the broiler chain is affected by the type of media used for isolation and enumeration.
ESBL/pAampC-EC were found in broiler production pyramid, that they are not dominant in the broiler intestine, and that carcasses are colonised with total E. coli, which may include ESBL/pAamC-EC.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the prevalence of ESBL- and AmpC-producing E. coli in an integrated broilers production chain, with special focus on the transmission of these bacteria from the farm to the slaughterhouse and the carcass.
the impact of selective and non- selective methods for the detection of ESBL/pAMPc-EC in the integrated broiler production pyramid.
the development of a better understanding of the prevalence and genetic makeup in the integrated broiler chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ESBL/pAampC-EC are present in the broiler chain, but their impact on individual hosts and carcasses is low, and the overall risk for humans is considered low.
the use of selective media is not a valid approach to estimate ESBL/pAmpsC-EC colonisations in broilers.
ESBL/pAmps-producing E. coli are widespread in the broiler food chain, but that they are subdominant in the gut, which is an important factor for the assessment of risk to human health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of selective media is not a reliable method for estimating the prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli in the broilers production pyramid.
the prevalence of ESBL-EC and pAmpC-ec in broilers is higher than previously thought.

the use of a selective method to estimate ESBL/pApc-producing E. coli prevalence in broiler production is not representative for the prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli at the isolate level and therefore not representative of the colonisation level of individual hosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of isolation media is a critical aspect of the study design, and should be carefully considered when assessing the risk of ESBL/pAMPc-producing bacteria in the food chain.
a combination of selective and nonselective approaches is necessary for a complete assessment of the impact of ESBL/pAMPc-EC on the broiler chain.
the use of non-selective media is a valuable addition to selective methods, as it enables to estimate prevalence at individual host level.
